logs: Review of gates: Not ready to report: 1 blocker, 11 major, 9 minor. All the checks pass, but they miss these defects; 13 probes in the scratchpad reproduced them against the real code. The blocker: the registered demo function takes no wait or retry, so survey-2's call fn(root, story, run, wait=..., retry=...) raises TypeError. The demo gate also never returns its own passing record for the head, so a later failing call overwrites it. It can return passed false with no failure line, answers ok true when admission is refused, and never lists a criterion with no test. Green returns a cached pass even when its .xml copy is gone, so demo fails at that head with no way out. The base report is written in place and a cut-off copy is read silently as empty. Exempt red tests count toward the half rule. The re-freeze refuses because of unchanged tests, and crashes on an error with no type and on an over-cap record. Interfaces missing promised fields: the cached green result has no changed_files, the green record has no diff_patch, and sha is empty on refusals made after the story resolved. The six fixed findings hold. The five left-for-builder entries were right.. 21 findings, 12 blocker or major.
Round 1 for gates: 20 of 21 fixes confirmed, 3 still open.
Round 2 for gates: 3 of 3 fixes confirmed, 1 still open.

still_open.problem: The S4R-gates-15 fix added build_suite, which loads each */test_*.py outside tests/ with loader.loadTestsFromModule(importlib.import_module(name)). An import error in such a file is not caught: the runner exits with a traceback and writes no build/junit.xml, even when tests/ holds tests it could report. A probe with tally/test_broken.py importing a missing module confirmed it: traceback, no build/ directory. The gate then reports 'the test command wrote no JUnit report' instead of the build or harness error. Discovery over tests/ turns the same import error into an ImportError test case. This breaks the runner's promise to write build/junit.xml after every run.
still_open.proposed_fix: Load each source-tree module with loader.loadTestsFromName(name). A probe showed that it turns the import error into a unittest.loader._FailedTest case with type="ImportError" and still writes the report. Add a unit test where a story commits an import-broken tally/test_*.py and red still reads a report.
